newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile court refuses to cut Letelier case sentence.
newsitem.headline: Chile court refuses to cut Letelier case sentence.

text.p: Chile's Supreme Court on Friday rejected an appeal by a former secret police chief to reduce his jail sentence for ordering the murder of exiled Socialist leader Orlando Letelier in Washington in 1976.
Retired army Gen. Manuel Contreras, Gen. Augusto Pinochet's secret police boss during the 1973-1990 military regime, sought to cut one year off his seven-year prison term, his lawyer said.

Contreras and his deputy, Pedro Espinoza, were jailed in 1995 for ordering the car-bomb assassination of Letelier in Washington, where the Chilean lived in exile following the military coup that overthrew Marxist President Salvador Allende.
Letelier's young American assistant Ronni Moffitt also died in the explosion in Washington's Sheridan Circle.

Contreras and Espinoza are in the Punta Peuco high security prison built to house military officers convicted of human rights abuses under Pinochet's government. The two ran DINA, the feared security service responsible for killing and torturing thousands of left-wing opponents in the early years of the Pinochet regime.
